 Vultr: Agent Rush Hackathon
 Build AI agents that do real work — safely sandboxed on Vultr.
 Online phase
 3 – 8 November, 2026
 On-site · Salt Lake City, UT
 8 November, 2026
 Prize pool
 $9,000 + $5,000 in credits
 Build a web-based agent that performs real work — writing and running code, or operating a real browser — with every action contained inside a sandbox running on Vultr.
 Your system acts as a centralized control layer: it plans a task, dispatches it to an isolated execution environment, and returns verifiable output. Projects should demonstrate multi-step agentic workflows, real executed results rather than described ones, and a production-style web application — all running on Vultr infrastructure.
 Containment-first is required. An agent that only chats is a demo; an agent that executes safely is a product.
 Every participant gets $200 in free Vultr credits to build on.
 Main challenge 
 Blast Radius Zero: Safe Agent Execution on Vultr
 Build a web-based agent that performs real work — writing and running code, or operating a real browser — with every action contained inside a sandbox running on Vultr. Your system should act as a centralized control layer that plans a task, dispatches it to an isolated execution environment, and returns verifiable output.
 Projects should demonstrate multi-step agentic workflows, real executed results rather than described ones, and a production-style web application, all running on Vultr infrastructure. Containment-first is required: an agent that only chats is a demo; an agent that executes safely is a product.
 Execution patterns — build against one or both
 Pattern A — Sandboxed code execution
 User asks → model writes code → code runs in a container → real output (chart, file, test log) returns → model explains it. On error, stderr is fed back for a retry.
 CSV Analyst — upload a spreadsheet, ask a question in plain English, get an actually-executed chart plus the code that produced it
 Prove-It Code Reviewer — paste a snippet or PR; the agent runs it and its tests in the sandbox and reports what really happened
 Chart Anything — natural language in, executed matplotlib or plotly image out
 File Fixer — messy CSV or JSON in, cleaned file out, with an executed before/after diff
 Self-Healing Runner — the agent runs code, reads the error, patches it, and retries, with the retry loop visible on screen
 Pattern B — Sandboxed browser use
 User gives a goal → model plans → Playwright in a container navigates, clicks, types → screenshots return → a vision model on Serverless Inference verifies the result → repeat, with a human approving anything final.
 Comparison Shopper — two or three product URLs in, screenshot-backed comparison table out
 Form Filler — structured data in, multi-step web form filled, with a screenshot trail and an approve-before-submit gate
 Site QA Sweep — point it at a web app and get back broken flows and links with screenshots and repro steps
 Research with Receipts — a brief where every claim links to a screenshot of its source
 Page Watcher — monitors listing or pricing pages, extracts structured data, and diffs against yesterday
 What we’re looking for
 Containment focus
 Address real safety and reliability challenges in agent execution, and show how isolation makes autonomous execution shippable.
 Process isolation — execution never touches the host or app runtime
 Secret hygiene — no API keys or credentials inside the sandbox
 Resource limits — time and memory caps on every run
 Lifecycle discipline — reset or destroy the environment after each task
 Production-ready web application
 Must be accessible via a public web browser
 Demonstrate a real product-style experience
 Clear user flows, not just a local demo
 Vultr is the central backend powering execution and orchestration. Your application plans, dispatches, and verifies real work — the focus is platform thinking, not a one-off demo.
 Developer expectations
 Each team must provide
 GitHub repository with setup and documentation
 Vultr VM backend deployment, with agent LLM calls through Vultr Serverless Inference
 Public demo URL
 Recorded demo video
 One containment moment in the video — the sandbox absorbing something unsafe, such as an rm -rf , an infinite loop, or a hostile web page
 Clear explanation of architecture and use case
 Additional tracks — to be announced
 Any further tracks and partner challenges will be published here before the kickoff.
 Partners 
 Partners
 Lead partner
 Vultr
 Vultr is an independent cloud computing platform on a mission to provide businesses and developers around the world with unrivaled ease of use, price-to-performance, and global reach.
 Vultr is a full-stack cloud compute and cloud GPU provider, offering bare metal, managed Kubernetes, managed databases, cloud storage and networking across its global data center regions, with a user-friendly control panel and API-first automation.
 Vultr VM backend Required 
 Deploy your backend on a Vultr VM and let it run the whole loop. Vultr should be the central system of control and orchestration, not just static hosting.
 Vultr Serverless Inference Required 
 All agent LLM calls must go through Vultr Serverless Inference. It is OpenAI-compatible, so point your client at the base URL https://api.vultrinference.com/v1 . Vision-capable models are available for reasoning over screenshots.
 Sandbox boundary Required 
 Sandboxes run as containers or throwaway instances on Vultr, never inside your app process. A Docker container as the sandbox boundary is strongly recommended; OpenSandbox, gVisor and E2B are open-source examples you can start from.
 Vultr API Optional 
 Use the Vultr API to spin up a throwaway instance per task and destroy it afterward, making Vultr itself the sandbox fabric.

 Guidelines 
 Guidelines
 How to participate
 The hackathon takes place online on the lablab.ai platform and the
 lablab.ai Discord server . Please register for both in order to participate. To join, click the Enroll button at the bottom of the page and read the Hackathon Guidelines , the
 Getting Started Guide 
 and the lablab.ai Hackathon Rule Book .
 Everyone is welcome to participate, regardless of previous AI or coding experience.
 Before the kickoff, browse the AI Tech and tutorials pages to read up on the available technologies and get a head start on your project.
 Teams
 Teams consist of 1-6 people. If you don't have a team, don't worry. You can connect with other participants from all over the world on the dashboard or on the
 Discord server , where you can also find teammates and bounce around ideas.
